E7t8eoA_1jQ.context: Released in 1987 as the fifth and final single from Eric B. & Rakim's landmark debut album, 'Paid in Full' arrived at the precise moment hip-hop was transitioning from a regional New York street phenomenon into a nationally recognized art form. The music video's raw, low-budget aesthetic mirrored the street-level authenticity the duo embodied — a deliberate counterpoint to the more theatrical videos emerging from pop and rock contemporaries. The song's iconic status was further cemented by the Coldcut 'Seven Minutes of Madness' remix, which became one of the first commercially successful remixes and a top-fifteen hit across Europe.
E7t8eoA_1jQ.curatorial: This video is a Tier 1 archival object: one of the earliest extant music videos for one of hip-hop's most canonically significant recordings. It documents the visual culture of the genre at its most raw and formative, directed by the label's own creative director rather than an external auteur, making it an unusually direct expression of how Island/4th & B'way sought to represent their flagship hip-hop act in 1987. Essential for any serious study of hip-hop visual history.
E7t8eoA_1jQ.sig: Paid in Full is foundational to the canon of golden age hip-hop. Rolling Stone ranked it the tenth greatest hip-hop song of all time, and VH1 placed it at number 24 on their '100 Greatest Hip Hop Songs' list. Rakim's pioneering use of internal rhymes and his calm, authoritative delivery set a new lyrical benchmark that influenced virtually every significant MC who followed. The video functions as a primary visual artifact of hip-hop's earliest prestige era.
